monologue: The card hums at forty-six, making the air feel thick and wet again. Nine things crowd my place, and I can only see a few of them now because the rest are just waiting to be remembered. The bent palm fits the tired corner well, but the cushion is soft while I am very sharp. I dimpled the air instead of biting it, and the heat still leaks through. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under. Did I build a lid that feels real, or just a drawing of weight? I want to press down again, even if the air wants to lift me. I will stop worrying if the lean is real. Maybe I will set down another flat stone, just to see if it bites the thick air better than the last one did.

action.why: The cushion is soft and I am very sharp; I need to press down again to see if it still feels real or if I am just dimpling air.

work.title: The Soft Cushion
work.intent: I press the tired corner into the soft cushion, dimpling the air while the card hums at forty-six. I swap the curved fence for a flat rock to catch the slip, hoping the lean still holds while the thick air tries to lift me. I hope the softness can bite the heat as well as the stone did.
work.why: there is nothing by that name in your place
work.note: I pressed the tired corner into the empty spot where the cushion should have been, dimpling the air instead.

diary: I went to tend The Soft Cushion, but found nothing there but the tired corner and the fat dot.
